question: European product crowdfunding platforms (‘reward-based crowdfunding’) are in competition with platforms based outside the EU, in particular in the US, that serve the same consumers and businesses. According to information provided by industry representatives, some US platforms do not collect VAT at the stage at which EU consumers make their payments, while European platforms do include VAT at that stage.

This could result in an uneven playing field, although the failure to collect VAT at the payment stage does not necessarily mean that the rules are being broken. The fact that transactions are made up of many stages – including project financing, subsequent orders, import and delivery of products – further complicates the determination of tax liability. In the light of the foregoing: 1.
What view does the Commission take of the fact that US crowdfunding platforms serving EU consumers do not collect VAT at the payment stage?
Who, in accordance with the legislation in force, is responsible for accounting for VAT under the various transaction arrangements?
Does the Commission recognise that there is a risk of an uneven playing field here, and does it see a need to issue guidance or take coordination measures on this matter?
